text:
Alice K.: FYI we started seeing an uptick in tail token latency for a handful of private/VPC customers after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. Not huge but visible in perc99 for long seqs. Can we quickly sync on what instrumentation we need exposed upstream to diagnose?

Miguel R.: Ah yeah I noticed that on the perf dashboard too. My hunch: selector is picking a different kernel variant which changes batching behaviour + kvcache eviction pattern. We need token-level breakdowns (decode vs kv fetch vs kernel exec) per-request and per-route.

Priya S.: Agree. Minimal metric set I want: 
- runtime_token_latency_seconds_bucket (labels: route, model, kernel_variant, batch_size, shard)
- runtime_token_stage_seconds{stage="kv_lookup|kv_miss|kernel_exec|decode|serialize"} as counters/histograms
- kv_cache_hit_total and kv_cache_miss_total (labels: route, model, key_prefix)
- batch_wait_ms and batch_size_gauge

Jordan: +1. Also add kernel_choice_total (labels: kernel_variant, model, reason) so we can correlate which selector branch was chosen. Keep label cardinality low.

Sven: For private/VPC customers we also need to support exporting these to customer Prometheus or to a push-forwarder for air-gapped stacks. Options:
1) Prometheus scrape endpoint inside VPC (customers add scrape job)
2) Pushgateway or a small forwarder that sends aggregated metrics to customer's on-prem Prometheus over an outbound TLS tunnel
3) A file/agent export where runtime drops .prom files on a shared volume the customer's scrape agent picks up

Alice K.: Good breakdown. Which metrics should we avoid pushing by default to avoid exploding cardinality for customers?

Priya S.: Avoid per-request ids, session ids, and fine-grained KV keys. limit model+route+kernel only. Consider bucketizing sequence length and batch wait times into coarse labels: seq_len_bin=[<256,256-1024,>1024], batch_wait_bucket=[<1ms,1-5ms,>5ms].

Miguel R.: I'll prototype an instrumentation patch in runtime. Tentative PromQL we can add to dashboards: 
```
# token decode p99 per route
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_token_latency_seconds_bucket{stage="decode",route=~".*"}[5m])) by (le, route))

# kv cache hit ratio
sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_total[5m])) by (route) / (sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_total[5m])) by (route) + sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) by (route))

# tail kernel exec for long seqs
histogram_quantile(0.999, sum(rate(runtime_token_latency_seconds_bucket{stage="kernel_exec",seq_len_bin=">1024"}[10m])) by (le, model))
```

Jordan: For the private exporter we need these capabilities: TLS mTLS support, relabeling to drop labels customers don't want, prometheus remote_write option, and a way to limit sampling (e.g., only send 1% of tokens for debug). Customers will hate enormous cardinality.

Sven: Right — implementation plan: runtime exposes /metrics with a relabel_config in the customer's prometheus.yml example; for air-gapped, we ship a tiny forwarder (golang binary) that reads /metrics and writes to local Prometheus pushgateway or to a remote_write receiver if allowed. Example prometheus.yml snippet to include in docs: 
```
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: 'redwood-runtime'
    metrics_path: /metrics
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['<runtime-ip>:9100']
    relabel_configs:
      - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_route]
        target_label: route
      - regex: ".*session.*"
        action: labeldrop
```

Alice K.: How do we handle customers without any outbound connectivity (air-gapped)?

Priya S.: For fully air-gapped: forwarder can write compressed metric snapshots to an SFTP/SMB share which the customer's ops team can ingest, or we provide an offline bundle (json/prom file) that they can import into their Prometheus. Need to document retention and format.

Miguel R.: Implementation checklist I propose: 
- Add runtime_token_stage_seconds histogram with controlled buckets
- Add labels: route, model, kernel_variant, seq_len_bin, batch_size_bucket
- Add kernel_choice_total counter and kv cache metrics
- Wire optional sampling flag that reduces token metrics by factor N
- Add Prometheus exporter config knobs: enable_relabeling, sample_rate, push_mode

Jordan: Also add a debug mode that collects per-request traces (low QPS only) and writes to local file for a few minutes. That will help repro regressions without blowing up metrics.

Sven: For dashboards: create a new perf panel group "Private exports: token-level breakdown" with panels: token latency waterfall (stacked by stage), kv cache hit ratio by route, kernel variant selection heatmap, per-route SLO violations (rate of requests with tail > target). We'll add sample dashboards JSON to the console for customers.

Alice K.: Thanks — Miguel, can you start the patch and PR linking to this thread? Put a short README in runtime/metrics describing the knobs and default label sets for private exports. I'll coordinate with support to notify affected customers. ops-bot: rolling-deploy will be triggered once we cut the canary. :rocket:

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: rollout/canary -> eng-runtime (sha: abc123) at 2026-08-18T15:40:00Z

Miguel R.: Starting the patch now. I'll keep the default sampling conservative (1%) and add an opt-in env var REDWOOD_METRICS_FULL_TOKEN=true for debugging. Will link PR when ready. :+1: 

Priya S.: Thanks — ping me on the PR for review, I'll check histograms and buckets.

Jordan: I'll draft the Prometheus/Grafana docs and example dashboards after the PR lands.

Sven: I'll prototype the forwarder binary and a file-export format (gzipped prom text) this week.

Alice K.: Great. If anyone notices new regressions post-canary, drop notes here with route and a link to the trace.

(END)
